title: Regista kernel workflow document
description: The authoring format for a workflow definition, loadable from YAML or JSON. This is the 0.8 kernel's dialect: a deliberately reduced form of the 0.7 schema (src/regista/_workflow_schema.json). Keys the 0.7 schema accepted and this one does not are refused by name with an explanation rather than ignored -- see WORKFLOW_DOCUMENT_REMOVED_KEYS in kernel.py -- because silently dropping 'allowed_roles' would drop a role restriction, and silently dropping 'validator' would drop a gate.
$comment: Two rules live in the loader, not here, because JSON Schema can state them only in a form that reports unhelpfully: exactly one state carries initial: true (contains/maxContains prints the entire states array back at you), and 'roles' is required if and only if a transition restricts to one.

kernel_workflow.description: Version of THIS DOCUMENT FORMAT -- not of the library, and not of the workflow. The registry assigns workflow versions; pinning a library version in a document is how 0.7's 'regista_version' ended up meaning nothing.

roles.description: The closed set of role names this workflow's transitions may restrict to. Required once any transition declares 'roles'. It exists to be cross-checked: a role named on a transition and nowhere else is a typo that would otherwise make that transition permanently un-performable, and the failure would surface only at runtime as a refusal naming a role nobody can present.

work_item_types.description: The closed set of work-item type names this workflow admits. create_work_item() refuses any other. Names only: the kernel validates no per-type custom-field declarations, so accepting the 0.7 object form would accept a declaration it does not enforce.

from.description: One source state, or several. Several sources belong under ONE entry: a transition name may appear only once in a document.

roles.description: Roles permitted to make this transition. Application policy: the kernel checks the role a caller PRESENTS against this list; it does not verify the caller holds it.

required_fields.description: Fields that must be present and non-null on the item once this transition has applied its own field changes.
